transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Location: Google Meet
Recorder: Fireflies
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE); Maya Singh (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Helios Eng Lead); Priya Raman (Helios PM); Luis Ortega (Helios SRE)
Links shared: runbook draft (internal link), pilot telemetry dashboard (helios-grafana link), load test spreadsheet (s3://helios-test-results/pilot-load.xlsx)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Final-week pilot sync. Focus: traffic shift plan (A/B -> canary -> full), monitoring thresholds, rollback triggers, runbooks, infra checks (VPC/KMS), and acceptance criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — let's do a quick roll call, then we'll run through telemetry and the proposed cutover playbook. Maya, you want to kick with the performance highlights?
[00:28] Maya: Yeah sure, uh so the last 72 hours we've seen steady throughput, basically average token throughput around 1.8k tps per instance, P95 latency was hovering around 180 to 210ms with bursts to 280ms on long-context prompts. Some of the spikes look correlated with the regen flows, and we still see cache misses on certain prefix patterns.
[01:05] Jordan: When you say "cache misses" — is that KV cache warmup? We've noticed worse latency on our agent prompts which include the 3-turn history.
[01:18] Maya: Right, it's mostly prefix/KV mismatch; the runtime evicts entries when sequence lengths jump. We're recommending short warmup sequences and keeping the common prefixes pinned in cache on the dedicated pool.
[01:33] Luis: Quick infra note — our peering added an extra hop for the first 10ms, so cold-starts look worse in our region. I'm checking with netops.
[01:49] Ethan: Good call. On the cutover plan itself, we proposed an A/B first — 10% traffic to Redwood variant and 90% to baseline for 2 hours, then a canary with progressive shifts 5->25->50 over 2 hours each if metrics stable. We need to confirm acceptance thresholds.
[02:15] Priya: For product, acceptance is two parts: quality and reliability. Quality: no regression in our 50-sample prompt set (we'll provide today). Reliability: P95 below 220ms and error rate < 0.5%. If either fails, automatic rollback.
[02:42] Maya: Sounds fine. I'd add a latency burn-in check at 10% and a slightly longer look at tail latency before moving to 25%. Also we'll validate model variant fallbacks — worker will fallback to quantized variant if memory pressure spikes.
[03:05] Jordan: How do we detect model-level issues vs infra issues? We don't want false positives and a noisy rollback.
[03:16] Maya: Good question. We'll rely on layered alerts: first, service-level errors (5xxs) then model-quality drift (BLEU-ish metric proxy for our use) and then infra signals (CPU/GPU memory, OOM). The runbook will include the triage checklist.
[03:35] Ethan: I'll paste the high-level runbook in chat right now — it's the one everyone saw in the deck with explicit Slack escalation channels. (link pasted)
[03:45] [file share by Ethan: https://redwood-docs/internal/runbooks/helios-cutover]
[04:01] Priya: Can you walk through the rollback steps? Our PMs want exact copy-and-paste commands so ops can run them quickly.
[04:12] Maya: Sure, at a high level: 1) stop traffic shift, 2) set routing weight back to baseline, 3) if model variant must change, call the pinned-model API to switch to the previous model version, 4) clear caches if necessary, 5) file incident ticket. I'll make the runbook commands explicit.
[04:33] Luis: For KMS — can you confirm Redwood only requests decrypt-only permissions for log decryption? We need to avoid key rotation issues.
[04:44] Ethan: Yes, decrypt-only for the test keys; production keys will be handled via customer-managed KMS with specific roles. We'll add the exact IAM policy snippet to the runbook.
[05:00] Jordan: Back to metrics — what's the safe window for observing canary before we escalate? If we do 10% for 2 hours that's a lot of time, but we prefer shorter.
[05:12] Maya: We can do a fast pass at 10% for 30 minutes for obvious fails (errors, big latency spikes), then a slightly longer 2-hour watch before major shifts. The issue is statistical power — for low-error-rate systems you need more traffic to be confident.
[05:34] Priya: We can accept staged durations: quick smoke then extended check. As long as it's documented.
[05:38] Ethan: Noted. On monitoring, we've added synthetic tests that run the 50 sample prompts and compare to baseline using a similarity/semantic drift score. If drift passes threshold, it's a pass. If DRIFT > 0.12 then fail.
[05:55] Jordan: That 0.12 number — can you explain? We've seen weirdness where paraphrases trip the metric.
[06:04] Maya: It's a relaxed threshold tuned to your dataset. We'll pair it with manual spot-checks during the canary. The manual gate will be Priya and Jordan doing spot checks on a short list.
[06:18] [06:18] Ethan: Action: Jordan to send the 50 prompts by EOD.
[06:22] Jordan: Will do.
[06:25] Maya: Another tuning note: batching configuration — we've set a max batch size to 32 for the pilot but we can increase to 48 if latency impact is small. That saves cost. We should run a quick sensitivity test.
[06:40] Luis: Cost side matters — our finance wants an estimate on incremental token costs for the pilot at 50% traffic.
[06:47] Ethan: We'll model that in a short spreadsheet, including expected percentage of cache hits. I'll send a rough cost delta by tomorrow.
[06:54] Priya: For canary automation, who's responsible for executing the traffic shifts? Do we want Redwood to control the routing or our infra?
[07:04] Maya: We recommend Redwood trigger the orchestrated traffic shift via our control API with customer confirmation. That reduces risk of misconfiguration on the customer side. But if Helios prefers to run it, we can hand-off the steps.
[07:18] Jordan: Prefer Redwood to run it for the first two canaries, then we'll take over.
[07:24] Ethan: That works. We'll require a two-person confirmation in Slack before each major shift.
[07:31] [08:00] Maya: Quick note on dedicated pool sizing — if we need faster tail latency, we recommend enabling pre-warm instances and using our reserved burst capacity for the cutover. That keeps cold-starts low.
[08:17] Luis: Pre-warm sounds good; what's the ops cost?
[08:21] Maya: Minimal incremental cost for the burst pool for a 4-hour window; we'll include estimated $$ in the cost delta.
[08:28] Priya: Are there any outstanding security audits we need to complete before cutover?
[08:33] Ethan: We have SOC2 artifacts ready; we still need a short SSO test — SAML assertion with your IdP — and KMS policy confirmation. We've added that as pre-cutover checklist items.
[08:44] Jordan: We also want a dry-run where we simulate rollback. Can we do a scheduled dry-run tomorrow?
[08:52] Maya: Yes, we can do a dry-run to simulate traffic-shift and rollback without touching production routing — basically replay on the staging control plane. We'll do that Thursday during the load test.
[09:02] Ethan: Great. Let's sync on schedule: load test and dry-run Thursday morning, Maya runs tests and posts results, Jordan reviews, final stakeholder sign-off on Friday, and then tentative cutover window Monday overnight? Priya, does Monday overnight work?
[09:20] Priya: Monday overnight is OK — we'll send calendar conflicts. We prefer early morning UTC window so we catch APAC traffic low.
[09:29] Ethan: Perfect.
[09:33] [12:00] Jordan: Small question: in your previous tests you mentioned quantized model variants — do we expect any quality delta when falling back?
[12:10] Maya: There is a small quality delta, usually a slight increase in perplexity and minor rewording differences. That's why we keep the fallback only for severe memory pressure or GPU OOMs. We'll flag the fallback in alerts so product can see when it occurred.
[12:25] Luis: For observability, can you push trace IDs back into our tracing pipeline? We want to correlate spikes with traces.
[12:32] Ethan: Yes, we can inject request IDs into response headers and pass them to your tracing endpoint. We'll document header key and sampling rules.
[12:44] Priya: Anything on SLOs we need to adjust for the pilot?
[12:49] Maya: For pilot, we suggest a provisional SLO: 99.5% success, P95 < 250ms. Post-gated we'll tighten to your target 99.9% and 220ms.
[12:58] Ethan: OK.
[13:05] [18:00] Maya: Quick note on telemetry retention — we keep finer resolution for 7 days by default; for the canary we can retain high-res for 14 days if you want to run deeper post-mortems.
[18:14] Jordan: Yes, increase retention for the cutover window.
[18:17] Ethan: Added.
[18:22] Priya: On communications: if rollback occurs, what's our customer-facing line? We need an internal message and a message for end-users.
[18:31] Maya: We'll prepare two templates: internal incident Slack and a short product notice that says "partial degradation, features affected: chat suggestions." We'll include fallback language.
[18:44] Ethan: I'll draft the templates and share.
[18:50] [22:00] Priya: Any final open risks?
[22:07] Luis: Network hop cold-starts, pending netops ticket.
[22:10] Jordan: Small chance of false positive drift alerts on paraphrase prompts.
[22:14] Maya: We'll mitigate both — netops ticket and manual spot-check gate.
[22:21] Ethan: Alright, recap: runbook update by Ethan, load tests by Maya Thursday, prompt set from Jordan, KMS/IAM from Luis, stakeholder review Friday, tentative cutover Monday morning UTC. Everyone ok?
[22:40] Priya: Yep.
[22:42] Jordan: Sounds good.
[22:44] Luis: Good.
[22:46] Maya: I'll send the load test commands and the warmup script after this call.
[22:53] Ethan: Thanks all. I'll send meeting notes and the updated runbook link. We'll reconvene if any blockers pop.
[22:59] End of transcript.
